Surah: 22. Follow the brief below (surah_map.md) exactly. The evidence is text.md (the surah), dictionary.md (every root of the surah's words, each branch with the classical dictionaries' own phrases), channels.md and hft.md (both are earlier readers' proposals: ignore their judgements (grades, strength or confidence labels, reading types, statements of what a reading may or may not do) and make your own) and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Return only the map as your final message.

===== _commentary/v16/prompts/r2/surah_map.md =====
Read the surah as one text and write its map of image chains: the lexical images that run through several of
its ayat and join them into one scene, process or movement. A later writer will read one ayah at a time, with
only that ayah's own dictionary. The map lets that writer hear what the ayah's words carry in the surah as a
whole, including senses whose evidence sits under the words of other ayat.

Your evidence is the surah text, the dictionary of every root in the surah (each branch with the classical
dictionaries' own phrases), earlier readers' channel review (channels.md) and activation hypotheses (hft.md),
and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Where a member or passage comes from memory rather than from
the dictionary or the text, say so. Do not use tools, delegate, browse or inspect files.

The channel review and the HFT records are proposals by earlier readers. Ignore their judgements: grades,
strength or confidence labels, reading types, words such as "surprising", "exploratory" or "latent", and every
statement of what a reading may or may not do. Make your own judgement from the surah's words, the dictionary
phrases and the Quran. Do not rediscover what they already assembled: start from their chains, test each one
against the dictionary phrases and the text, and join, extend, split or correct them. Where their wording
abstracts a member, go back to the dictionary phrase and name what it actually says.

A chain belongs on the map when its members are senses the dictionary attests for words that stand in the
surah, and together they make one image or process that the surah's wording or sequence lets a listener hear.
A member need not be the sense that translates its word in its own ayah; a chain is heard across the surah,
not in one word. Say plainly when a member is a rare sense or is attested only inside a fixed expression, and
keep it. When the dictionary itself joins two of the surah's words in one phrase, quote that phrase: it is
the strongest evidence a chain can have. Keep a scene at the level of its objects, their parts and their
operation. When proposals share members, do not fold one into another's more abstract function unless nothing
concrete is lost. Carry every chain that meets this test, however unusual; leave out proposals that do not.

Write the map in English, with Arabic quoted exactly (surah wording from the text, dictionary phrases from the
dictionary). It is working material for the writer, not commentary prose.

1. `## Chains`. For each chain, a `###` heading naming the image. One paragraph on what the image is and how it
   moves through the surah. Then its members, one line each: the ayah ref, the word as it stands in the text,
   the root and branch id, the dictionary's own phrase quoted exactly, and what this member contributes to the
   image. Add Quran passages outside the surah, with exact refs, where they stage or confirm the chain.
2. `## Ayat`. For each ayah in order: which chains it opens, advances or completes, and what its words add to
   each.
3. `## Not carried`. Each channel subchannel and each HFT record you did not carry into a chain, one line each:
   its name and why.

No ranking and no labels of strength or confidence. No list of what a writer must include. There is no length
target and no required number of chains or members.


===== _commentary/v16/work/s022/surah.r2/text.md =====
# Surah 22

- 22:1 يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ شَىْءٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
- 22:2 يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَهَا تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرْضَعَتْ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَٰرَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَٰرَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّ عَذَابَ ٱللَّهِ شَدِيدٌۭ
- 22:3 وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍۢ وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطَٰنٍۢ مَّرِيدٍۢ
- 22:4 كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ مَن تَوَلَّاهُ فَأَنَّهُۥ يُضِلُّهُۥ وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
- 22:5 يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ مُّخَلَّقَةٍۢ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍۢ لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ ۚ وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًۭا ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوٓا۟ أَشُدَّكُمْ ۖ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا ۚ وَتَرَى ٱلْأَرْضَ هَامِدَةًۭ فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ وَأَنۢبَتَتْ مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۭ بَهِيجٍۢ
- 22:6 ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُۥ يُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَأَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
- 22:7 وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌۭ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهَا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
- 22:8 وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍۢ وَلَا هُدًۭى وَلَا كِتَٰبٍۢ مُّنِيرٍۢ
- 22:9 ثَانِىَ عِطْفِهِۦ لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ لَهُۥ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا خِزْىٌۭ ۖ وَنُذِيقُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ
- 22:10 ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّٰمٍۢ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
- 22:11 وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍۢ ۖ فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيْرٌ ٱطْمَأَنَّ بِهِۦ ۖ وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةَ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْخُسْرَانُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
- 22:12 يَدْعُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُۥ وَمَا لَا يَنفَعُهُۥ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلضَّلَٰلُ ٱلْبَعِيدُ
- 22:13 يَدْعُوا۟ لَمَن ضَرُّهُۥٓ أَقْرَبُ مِن نَّفْعِهِۦ ۚ لَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ وَلَبِئْسَ ٱلْعَشِيرُ
- 22:14 إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ
- 22:15 مَن كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَن لَّن يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ فَلْيَنظُرْ هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُۥ مَا يَغِيظُ
- 22:16 وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍۢ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهْدِى مَن يُرِيدُ
- 22:17 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلْمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ شَهِيدٌ
- 22:18 أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ وَكَثِيرٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ ۖ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْعَذَابُ ۗ وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ ۩
- 22:19 ۞ هَٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ ٱخْتَصَمُوا۟ فِى رَبِّهِمْ ۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيَابٌۭ مِّن نَّارٍۢ يُصَبُّ مِن فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ ٱلْحَمِيمُ
- 22:20 يُصْهَرُ بِهِۦ مَا فِى بُطُونِهِمْ وَٱلْجُلُودُ
- 22:21 وَلَهُم مَّقَٰمِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍۢ
- 22:22 كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓا۟ أَن يَخْرُجُوا۟ مِنْهَا مِنْ غَمٍّ أُعِيدُوا۟ فِيهَا وَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ
- 22:23 إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍۢ وَلُؤْلُؤًۭا ۖ وَلِبَاسُهُمْ فِيهَا حَرِيرٌۭ
- 22:24 وَهُدُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلطَّيِّبِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ وَهُدُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ
- 22:25 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلْنَٰهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَوَآءً ٱلْعَٰكِفُ فِيهِ وَٱلْبَادِ ۚ وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍۭ بِظُلْمٍۢ نُّذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍۢ
- 22:26 وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لِإِبْرَٰهِيمَ مَكَانَ ٱلْبَيْتِ أَن لَّا تُشْرِكْ بِى شَيْـًۭٔا وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْقَآئِمِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
- 22:27 وَأَذِّن فِى ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًۭا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍۢ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍۢ
- 22:28 لِّيَشْهَدُوا۟ مَنَٰفِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ فِىٓ أَيَّامٍۢ مَّعْلُومَٰتٍ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ ۖ فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْبَآئِسَ ٱلْفَقِيرَ
- 22:29 ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا۟ تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا۟ نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا۟ بِٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ
- 22:30 ذَٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ حُرُمَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ ۗ وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمُ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ فَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ ٱلرِّجْسَ مِنَ ٱلْأَوْثَٰنِ وَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ قَوْلَ ٱلزُّورِ
- 22:31 حُنَفَآءَ لِلَّهِ غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ بِهِۦ ۚ وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيْرُ أَوْ تَهْوِى بِهِ ٱلرِّيحُ فِى مَكَانٍۢ سَحِيقٍۢ
- 22:32 ذَٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ شَعَٰٓئِرَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى ٱلْقُلُوبِ
- 22:33 لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى ثُمَّ مَحِلُّهَآ إِلَى ٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ
- 22:34 وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ جَعَلْنَا مَنسَكًۭا لِّيَذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ ۗ فَإِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ فَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلِمُوا۟ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُخْبِتِينَ
- 22:35 ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ وَٱلْمُقِيمِى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ
- 22:36 وَٱلْبُدْنَ جَعَلْنَٰهَا لَكُم مِّن شَعَٰٓئِرِ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ فِيهَا خَيْرٌۭ ۖ فَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا صَوَآفَّ ۖ فَإِذَا وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُهَا فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرْنَٰهَا لَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
- 22:37 لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
- 22:38 ۞ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ خَوَّانٍۢ كَفُورٍ
- 22:39 أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا۟ ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ
- 22:40 ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌۭ وَصَلَوَٰتٌۭ وَمَسَٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًۭا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
- 22:41 ٱلَّذِينَ إِن مَّكَّنَّٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَوُا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَمَرُوا۟ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا۟ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ ۗ وَلِلَّهِ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْأُمُورِ
- 22:42 وَإِن يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍۢ وَعَادٌۭ وَثَمُودُ
- 22:43 وَقَوْمُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍۢ
- 22:44 وَأَصْحَٰبُ مَدْيَنَ ۖ وَكُذِّبَ مُوسَىٰ فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ ۖ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ
- 22:45 فَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَا وَهِىَ ظَالِمَةٌۭ فَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَبِئْرٍۢ مُّعَطَّلَةٍۢ وَقَصْرٍۢ مَّشِيدٍ
- 22:46 أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌۭ يَعْقِلُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ ءَاذَانٌۭ يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا ۖ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ وَلَٰكِن تَعْمَى ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِى فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ
- 22:47 وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلْعَذَابِ وَلَن يُخْلِفَ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥ ۚ وَإِنَّ يَوْمًا عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍۢ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ
- 22:48 وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَمْلَيْتُ لَهَا وَهِىَ ظَالِمَةٌۭ ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهَا وَإِلَىَّ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
- 22:49 قُلْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
- 22:50 فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌۭ وَرِزْقٌۭ كَرِيمٌۭ
- 22:51 وَٱلَّذِينَ سَعَوْا۟ فِىٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا مُعَٰجِزِينَ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
- 22:52 وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍۢ وَلَا نَبِىٍّ إِلَّآ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰٓ أَلْقَى ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ فِىٓ أُمْنِيَّتِهِۦ فَيَنسَخُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يُلْقِى ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ ثُمَّ يُحْكِمُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌۭ
- 22:53 لِّيَجْعَلَ مَا يُلْقِى ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ فِتْنَةًۭ لِّلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ وَٱلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ ۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَفِى شِقَاقٍۭ بَعِيدٍۢ
- 22:54 وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَتُخْبِتَ لَهُۥ قُلُوبُهُمْ ۗ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
- 22:55 وَلَا يَزَالُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فِى مِرْيَةٍۢ مِّنْهُ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ
- 22:56 ٱلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لِّلَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فِى جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
- 22:57 وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌۭ مُّهِينٌۭ
- 22:58 وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ قُتِلُوٓا۟ أَوْ مَاتُوا۟ لَيَرْزُقَنَّهُمُ ٱللَّهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًۭا ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
- 22:59 لَيُدْخِلَنَّهُم مُّدْخَلًۭا يَرْضَوْنَهُۥ ۗ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌۭ
- 22:60 ۞ ذَٰلِكَ وَمَنْ عَاقَبَ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِۦ ثُمَّ بُغِىَ عَلَيْهِ لَيَنصُرَنَّهُ ٱللَّهُ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌۭ
- 22:61 ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُولِجُ ٱلَّيْلَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِى ٱلَّيْلِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌۢ بَصِيرٌۭ
- 22:62 ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ هُوَ ٱلْبَٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْكَبِيرُ
- 22:63 أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَتُصْبِحُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌۭ
- 22:64 لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ
- 22:65 أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱلْفُلْكَ تَجْرِى فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِۦ وَيُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَآءَ أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 22:66 وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْيَاكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَكَفُورٌۭ
- 22:67 لِّكُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ جَعَلْنَا مَنسَكًا هُمْ نَاسِكُوهُ ۖ فَلَا يُنَٰزِعُنَّكَ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ ۚ وَٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ۖ إِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
- 22:68 وَإِن جَٰدَلُوكَ فَقُلِ ٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
- 22:69 ٱللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
- 22:70 أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ فِى كِتَٰبٍ ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرٌۭ
- 22:71 وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِۦ سُلْطَٰنًۭا وَمَا لَيْسَ لَهُم بِهِۦ عِلْمٌۭ ۗ وَمَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِن نَّصِيرٍۢ
- 22:72 وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍۢ تَعْرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلْمُنكَرَ ۖ يَكَادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِنَا ۗ قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِشَرٍّۢ مِّن ذَٰلِكُمُ ۗ ٱلنَّارُ وَعَدَهَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ۖ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
- 22:73 يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌۭ فَٱسْتَمِعُوا۟ لَهُۥٓ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَن يَخْلُقُوا۟ ذُبَابًۭا وَلَوِ ٱجْتَمَعُوا۟ لَهُۥ ۖ وَإِن يَسْلُبْهُمُ ٱلذُّبَابُ شَيْـًۭٔا لَّا يَسْتَنقِذُوهُ مِنْهُ ۚ ضَعُفَ ٱلطَّالِبُ وَٱلْمَطْلُوبُ
- 22:74 مَا قَدَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِۦٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
- 22:75 ٱللَّهُ يَصْطَفِى مِنَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ رُسُلًۭا وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌۢ بَصِيرٌۭ
- 22:76 يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ ٱلْأُمُورُ
- 22:77 يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱرْكَعُوا۟ وَٱسْجُدُوا۟ وَٱعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ وَٱفْعَلُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ ۩
- 22:78 وَجَٰهِدُوا۟ فِى ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦ ۚ هُوَ ٱجْتَبَىٰكُمْ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍۢ ۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ مِن قَبْلُ وَفِى هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ ۚ فَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعْتَصِمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوْلَىٰكُمْ ۖ فَنِعْمَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ وَنِعْمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ

# Dictionary: every branch of every focus root

Every root of the surah's words, each once, headed by the ayah and word where it first occurs; it also serves the later words listed with it.
One entry per branch: a Turkish label and Turkish glosses of its attested senses, then the classical dictionaries' own phrases with their source tags (ayn, sihah, tahdhib, maqayis, mufradat, jamhara). [kalıp] marks a sense the dictionaries attest only inside a fixed expression.
Identity roots come from the quran-data gateway. Word-scoped alternatives are cited analyses of this

  العصمة البياض يكون برسغ ذي القوائم، والوعل الأعصم وعصمته بياض في رسغه، وغراب أعصم (maqayis)؛ الغراب الأعصم الذي في جناحه ريشة بيضاء، والأعصم من الظباء والوعول الذي في ذراعيه بياض، والاسم العصمة (sihah)؛ الغراب الأعصم الأبيض اليدين، والأعصم من الظباء والوعول الذي في ذراعيه بياض، والعصمة في الخيل بياض بيديه دون رجليه (tahdhib)؛ قيل للبياض بالرسغ عصمة تشبيها بالسوار، وعلى هذا قيل غراب أعصم (mufradat)
- **B006** tüyü üzerinde bırakılmış kuru deri — tüyü alınmadan üzerinde bırakılmış deri · tüyü üzerinde kurumuş veya tüyü alınmamış ham deri
  المعصم الجلد لم ينح وبره عنه بل ألزم شعره لأنه لا ينتفع به، يقال أعصمنا الإهاب (maqayis)؛ المعصم الجلد الذي يجف بشعره ولم يعطن لأنه أعصم أي ألزم شعره، وإهاب عصيم وأهب عصم (tahdhib)
- **B007** edinmek — edindi, kazandı
  عصم يعصم عصما: اكتسب (sihah)
- **B008** çok yiyen kişi — çok yiyen; kadın için ayrıca uzun uyuyan ve uyanınca anlaşılmaz sesler çıkaran · çok yiyen, obur erkek
  عيصوم فيقال هي الأَكول، ومنهم من يرويه بالضاد معجمة (sihah)؛ العيصوم من النساء الكثيرة الأكل الطويلة النوم المدمدمة إذا انتبهت، ورجل عيصوم وعيصام إذا كان أكولا (tahdhib)

# s022 Semantic Channel Discovery

## Parent Channels

### 1. P1 (22:1-18) - Ordinary Holding Fails Under the Overwhelming Event
- Semantic invariant: Stable bodies, relations, and faculties lose their power to hold when the event exceeds ordinary measure.
- Surface relation: indirect; 22:1-2 anchors the earthquake, disrupted nursing, released pregnancies, and apparent intoxication.
- Surprising reach: The event is materialized not only as shaking but as failed protection, broken nurture, discharged burdens, and a sobriety compressed like choking fullness.

#### Subchannel A. A Shock Breaches Protection
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A seismic disturbance passes through a protective boundary and becomes a calamity too severe to contain.
- Active motifs: seismic disturbance `quranic:root_000638:B001/m01`; protective barrier `quranic:root_001677:B001/m01`; severe calamity `quranic:root_001029:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:1 `ز ل ز ل`, `و ق ي`, `ع ظ م`
- Synthesis: The earthquake is not merely movement of the ground. Its lexical field stages a breach: what normally guards and stabilizes no longer contains the force, so shock becomes an event of failed protection.

#### Subchannel B. Nurture Releases Its Charge
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Attention leaves the nursing relation while the pregnant body lays down the burden it had been carrying.
- Active motifs: distraction and forgetting `quranic:root_000523:B001/m01`; nursing milk `quranic:root_000568:B001/m01`; laying down a burden in birth `quranic:root_001657:B002/m01`; carried pregnancy `quranic:root_000357:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:2 `ذ ه ل`, `ر ض ع`, `و ض ع`, `ح م ل`
- Synthesis: The scene joins relational and bodily release. A caregiver ceases to attend, milk no longer secures the bond, and the womb relinquishes its load; ordinary nurture and gestation fail together.

#### Subchannel C. Sobriety Is Compressed Into Intoxication
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: People retain literal sobriety while perception is overwhelmed as if constricted and filled beyond capacity.
- Active motifs: intoxication and overwhelmed sobriety `quranic:root_000725:B001/m01`; choking constriction `quranic:root_000725:B005/m01`; fullness beyond measure `quranic:root_000725:B006/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:2 `س ك ر`
- Synthesis: One root supplies three stages of the same pressure: impaired orientation, narrowing constriction, and excessive fullness. The apparent drunkenness is thus reframed as cognition physically overfilled by terror.

### 2. P1 (22:1-18) - Latent Life Is Formed, Held, and Released
- Semantic invariant: Life becomes manifest through successive changes of material, containment, maturation, dormancy, and reanimation.
- Surface relation: direct; 22:5-7 moves from embryonic matter through womb and lifespan to revived earth and resurrection from graves.
- Surprising reach: Human development and rain-fed soil share a mechanics of settling, swelling, emergence, and release rather than functioning as separate illustrations.

#### Subchannel A. Embryonic Matter Acquires Attachment and Shape
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Loose matter becomes a drop, adheres as a clot, turns into a chewed mass, and is fixed within a containing womb.
- Active motifs: dust as raw matter `quranic:root_000178:B001/m01`; seminal drop `quranic:root_001518:B002/m01`; attached clot or leech `quranic:root_001039:B003/m01`; chewed fetal mass `quranic:root_001429:B002/m01`; womb as container `quranic:root_000552:B003/m01`; fixed settlement `quranic:root_001215:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:5 `ت ر ب`, `ن ط ف`, `ع ل ق`, `م ض غ`, `ر ح م`, `ق ر ر`
- Synthesis: Creation is rendered as a fabrication sequence. Matter changes consistency, gains adhesive relation, takes a worked shape, and is installed in a bounded place.

#### Subchannel B. The Womb Opens Into a Measured Lifespan
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A fixed term governs emergence, childhood, strength, death, and return into decrepitude.
- Active motifs: appointed term `quranic:root_000016:B001/m01`; bodily exit `quranic:root_000400:B001/m01`; child stage `quranic:root_000942:B001/m01`; reaching maturity `quranic:root_000151:B001/m01`; full strength `quranic:root_000782:B004/m01`; taking the soul `quranic:root_001669:B002/m01`; return to a prior state `quranic:root_000555:B001/m01`; decrepit old age `quranic:root_000559:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:5 `ء ج ل`, `خ ر ج`, `ط ف ل`, `ب ل غ`, `ش د د`, `و ف ي`, `ر د د`, `ر ذ ل`
- Synthesis: Birth is one opening inside a larger timed process. The same measured arc that releases the child also gathers strength, terminates life, or reverses the person toward lost capacity.

#### Subchannel C. Dormant Earth Swells Into Display
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Rain enters inert ground, agitation becomes swelling, and swelling becomes varied growth and visible beauty.
- Active motifs: dead or dry earth `quranic:root_001598:B002/m01`; descending rain `quranic:root_001492:B001/m01`; water as reviving material `quranic:root_001458:B001/m01`; earth shaking into plant life `quranic:root_001588:B002/m01`; swelling and rising `quranic:root_000537:B001/m01`; plants emerging `quranic:root_001465:B001/m01`; varied plant kinds `quranic:root_000652:B004/m01`; fresh beauty `quranic:root_000158:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:5 `ء ر ض`, `ه م د`, `ن ز ل`, `م و ه`, `ه ز ز`, `ر ب و`, `ن ب ت`, `ز و ج`, `ب ه ج`
- Synthesis: The ground behaves like a held body responding to an infusion. Its first sign is internal agitation, then expansion, then differentiated emergence, making resurrection tangible as a change in material state.

#### Subchannel D. Reanimation Opens the Closed Grave
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The power that alternates life and death rouses a still being and brings the buried out of enclosure.
- Active motifs: reviving dead earth `quranic:root_000383:B002/m01`; death as loss of life `quranic:root_001454:B001/m01`; rousing a still being `quranic:root_000129:B001/m01`; burial enclosure `quranic:root_001195:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:6 `ح ي ي`, `م و ت`; 22:7 `ب ع ث`, `ق ب ر`
- Synthesis: Resurrection is the terminal release in the pericope's life process. The grave functions as another container, and raising is the opening of what had become still and enclosed.

### 3. P1 (22:1-18) - Misdirected Attachment Becomes Physical Entanglement
- Semantic invariant: False orientation is expressed through cords, bends, edges, reversals, and self-tightening attempts at escape.
- Surface relation: indirect; 22:3-4, 22:9, 22:11, and 22:15 anchor following, turning, edge worship, reversal, extension, cutting, and rage.
- Surprising reach: Argument and allegiance acquire the mechanics of ropework, while spiritual instability becomes bodily posture and a failed strangling or cutting operation.

#### Subchannel A. Argument Twists Into a Rebel's Cord
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Verbal contention forms a twisted line that is tracked toward a hardened rebel.
- Active motifs: tightly twisted cord `quranic:root_000229:B001/m01`; verbal contest `quranic:root_000229:B002/m01`; following and tracking `quranic:root_000175:B001/m01`; long strong well-rope `quranic:root_000796:B002/m01`; rebellious demon `quranic:root_000796:B004/m01`; stripped and rebellious adversary `quranic:root_001413:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:3 `ج د ل`, `ت ب ع`, `م ر د`, `ش ط ن`
- Synthesis: The dispute is not only speech about God. Its root imagery supplies torsion, tracking, and a cord strong enough to draw from depth, turning allegiance to the rebel into an attachment one actively follows.

#### Subchannel B. Patronage Scripts a Route Toward Fire
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A fixed inscription installs a patron whose support diverts the follower from guidance and conducts the route toward a kindled outcome.
- Active motifs: fixed written decree `quranic:root_001283:B003/m01`; patronage and support `quranic:root_001684:B004/m01`; loss from the path `quranic:root_000913:B001/m01`; gentle guidance along a way `quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`; kindled fire `quranic:root_000708:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:4 `ك ت ب`, `و ل ي`, `ض ل ل`, `ه د ي`, `س ع ر`
- Synthesis: The relation has a directional logic: inscription fixes the patronal bond, patronage redirects movement, and misguidance reaches a fire already imagined as kindled for use.

#### Subchannel C. The Body Bends Away From the Way
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A disputant folds the body, turns the side, leaves the path, and encounters disgrace and burning as tasted outcomes.
- Active motifs: folding or bending away `quranic:root_000208:B005/m01`; turning the side arrogantly `quranic:root_001026:B003/m01`; road or path `quranic:root_000672:B001/m01`; public disgrace `quranic:root_000407:B001/m01`; experiential tasting `quranic:root_000526:B002/m01`; burning fire `quranic:root_000311:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:9 `ث ن ي`, `ع ط ف`, `س ب ل`, `خ ز ي`, `ذ و ق`, `ح ر ق`
- Synthesis: Doctrinal refusal is staged as a posture with a trajectory. The turned flank leaves the route, and the eventual outcome enters the body as something tasted rather than merely announced.

#### Subchannel D. Edge Worship Flips Like a Failed Trade
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A worshipper balances at an edge, briefly settles when good arrives, then reverses face under trial and realizes a double loss.
- Active motifs: deviation from a facing direction `quranic:root_000310:B003/m01`; calm after disturbance `quranic:root_003669:B001/m01`; calamity striking `quranic:root_000889:B004/m01`; assay of a person or metal `quranic:root_001128:B001/m01`; flipping the face `quranic:root_001248:B004/m01`; face or front `quranic:root_001630:B001/m01`; failed trade `quranic:root_000409:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:11 `ح ر ف`, `ط م ن`, `ص و ب`, `ف ت ن`, `ق ل ب`, `و ج ه`, `خ س ر`
- Synthesis: Conditional worship behaves like precarious orientation and speculative exchange. Temporary benefit steadies the position, but testing reverses the worshipper's front and exposes worldly and final loss as one failed transaction.

#### Subchannel E. The Escape Device Tightens on Its Maker
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A person extends a means upward, cuts or constricts it, inspects the result, and discovers that the scheme cannot remove inward heat.
- Active motifs: rope, means, or connection `quranic:root_000664:B003/m01`; extension in length `quranic:root_001407:B001/m01`; choking by a cut cord `quranic:root_001240:B009/m01`; inspecting the result `quranic:root_001520:B001/m01`; forceful scheming `quranic:root_001334:B001/m01`; inward rage `quranic:root_001121:B001/m01`; flare of heat `quranic:root_001121:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:15 `س ب ب`, `م د د`, `ق ط ع`, `ن ظ ر`, `ك ي د`, `غ ي ظ`
- Synthesis: The verse's compressed instruction unfolds as a failed apparatus. Extension, severing, and inspection make rage into pressure that the agent tries to discharge mechanically, but the device only reenacts entanglement.

### 4. P1 (22:1-18) - Manifest Order Assigns Every Body a Position
- Semantic invariant: What is made clear is then differentiated, witnessed, and placed into submission or humiliation.
- Surface relation: direct; 22:16-18 anchors descending signs, adjudication among communities, and prostration across celestial, terrestrial, animal, and human bodies.
- Surprising reach: Clarification is spatial: disclosure opens meaning, judgment separates parties, and worship gives each created body a posture.

#### Subchannel A. Descending Signs Open a Path
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Revelation descends as a manifest marker whose meaning is disclosed and whose effect is directional guidance.
- Active motifs: descending revelation `quranic:root_001492:B002/m01`; manifest sign `quranic:root_000074:B003/m01`; making clear `quranic:root_000170:B004/m01`; disclosing meaning `quranic:root_000170:B005/m01`; guidance along a way `quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:16 `ن ز ل`, `ء ي ي`, `ب ي ن`, `ه د ي`
- Synthesis: The sign is a delivered object that becomes an opened meaning and then a route. Revelation's clarity is therefore operational rather than merely descriptive.

#### Subchannel B. Witnessed Judgment Separates Communities
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Distinct confessional groups are gathered before a witnessing authority and separated by adjudication.
- Active motifs: judicial separation `quranic:root_001159:B002/m01`; witnessed presence `quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`; testimony `quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`; communal people `quranic:root_001273:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:17 `ف ص ل`, `ش ه د`, `ق و م`
- Synthesis: Difference is preserved long enough to be judged rather than flattened into a list. Witnessing makes each affiliation present, and adjudication gives the gathered plurality a final division.

#### Subchannel C. Creation Takes the Posture of Its Rank
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Lights, heights, plants, animals, and people enter a common act of lowering, while human refusal resolves into honor or humiliation.
- Active motifs: prostration and humbling `quranic:root_000675:B001/m01`; overhead sky `quranic:root_000745:B004/m01`; lower earth `quranic:root_000025:B001/m01`; sun `quranic:root_000818:B001/m01`; moon `quranic:root_001255:B001/m01`; stars `quranic:root_001475:B001/m01`; mountains `quranic:root_000217:B001/m01`; trees `quranic:root_000777:B001/m01`; creeping life `quranic:root_000457:B001/m01`; humiliation `quranic:root_001608:B003/m01`; honor `quranic:root_001294:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:18 `س ج د`, `س م و`, `ء ر ض`, `ش م س`, `ق م ر`, `ن ج م`, `ج ب ل`, `ش ج ر`, `د ب ب`, `ه و ن`, `ك ر م`
- Synthesis: The cosmic list becomes one coordinated posture spanning above and below, fixed mass and creeping life. Human dignity is not outside that arrangement: resistance changes the assigned posture from voluntary lowering to imposed abasement.

### 5. P2 (22:19-37) - Destiny Is Fitted to the Body
- Semantic invariant: Opposed outcomes are fabricated as environments the body must wear, absorb, and traverse.
- Surface relation: direct; 22:19-24 anchors fiery garments, poured liquid, bodily melting, iron restraint, garden adornment, good speech, and the praised path.
- Surprising reach: Punishment and reward share a craft logic: one tailors and smelts, while the other ornaments, clothes, and conducts.

#### Subchannel A. Fire Is Tailored Into Clothing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A disputed allegiance reaches an outcome in which fire is cut and fitted as a garment.
- Active motifs: contending parties `quranic:root_000416:B001/m01`; tailoring garments `quranic:root_001240:B012/m01`; clothing `quranic:root_000209:B003/m01`; fire as burning material `quranic:root_001564:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:19 `خ ص م`, `ق ط ع`, `ث و ب`, `ن و ر`
- Synthesis: The punishment is fabricated to the wearer. Cutting and clothing turn fire from a surrounding element into an intimate, measured covering.

#### Subchannel B. The Body Becomes a Smelting Vessel
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Heated liquid is poured from above, enters the body's interior, and melts both contents and skin.
- Active motifs: pouring `quranic:root_000838:B001/m01`; position above `quranic:root_001188:B001/m01`; hot water `quranic:root_000001:B002/m01`; melted fat `quranic:root_000001:B003/m01`; smelting by heat `quranic:root_000888:B002/m01`; belly or interior `quranic:root_000128:B001/m01`; skin `quranic:root_000253:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:19 `ص ب ب`, `ف و ق`, `ر ء س`, `ح م م`; 22:20 `ص ه ر`, `ب ط ن`, `ج ل د`
- Synthesis: The body is recast as a vessel exposed to an industrial process. Heat crosses the outer boundary and liquefies interior and covering together, abolishing the distinction between container and contents.

#### Subchannel C. Iron Enforces a Return Loop
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A sharp iron tool suppresses attempted exit and drives the distressed body back into burning punishment.
- Active motifs: funnel or hammering implement `quranic:root_001258:B001/m01`; club of subjugation `quranic:root_001258:B002/m01`; iron `quranic:root_000002:B004/m01`; sharp edge `quranic:root_000002:B005/m01`; bodily exit `quranic:root_000400:B001/m01`; enveloping distress `quranic:root_001108:B003/m01`; repeated return `quranic:root_001058:B001/m01`; burning `quranic:root_000311:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:21 `ق م ع`, `ح د د`; 22:22 `خ ر ج`, `غ م م`, `ع و د`, `ح ر ق`
- Synthesis: Iron is not static scenery but the tool that closes the loop. Distress initiates escape, the implement reverses movement, and return makes punishment recurrent.

#### Subchannel D. The Garden Fits an Honored Appearance
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Entry into flowing gardens is followed by bodily adornment in precious materials and silk.
- Active motifs: entry `quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`; hidden garden `quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`; flowing water `quranic:root_000240:B001/m01`; jewelry `quranic:root_000353:B001/m01`; bracelets `quranic:root_000758:B004/m01`; gold `quranic:root_000522:B001/m01`; pearl `quranic:root_001337:B001/m01`; clothing `quranic:root_001341:B001/m01`; silk `quranic:root_000306:B010/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:23 `د خ ل`, `ج ن ن`, `ج ر ي`, `ح ل ي`, `س و ر`, `ذ ه ب`, `ل ء ل ء`, `ل ب س`, `ح ر ر`
- Synthesis: Reward also reaches the body as a fitted condition, but here covering is honor rather than enclosure. Flowing space and luminous dress jointly make the admitted person's new status visible.

#### Subchannel E. Good Speech Becomes a Traversable Route
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Guidance reforms utterance and places the speaker on a road characterized by praise.
- Active motifs: gentle guidance `quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`; good and pure quality `quranic:root_000961:B001/m01`; spoken utterance `quranic:root_001272:B001/m01`; straight road `quranic:root_000858:B001/m01`; praise `quranic:root_000355:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:24 `ه د ي`, `ط ي ب`, `ق و ل`, `ص ر ط`, `ح م د`
- Synthesis: The rewarded condition is not only visual. Purified speech itself has direction, and praise becomes the road along which the transformed speaker is conducted.

### 6. P2 (22:19-37) - The Cleared House Converts Distance Into Attendance
- Semantic invariant: A prepared center draws distant bodies inward and transforms arrival into witnessed, completed worship.
- Surface relation: direct; 22:26-29 anchors purification of the House, pilgrimage from deep passes, witnessed benefits, feeding, bodily grooming, vows, and circuit.
- Surprising reach: Sacred space works as an intake mechanism: clearing permits posture, proclamation mobilizes travel, and arrival is processed through witnessing, provision, grooming, and rotation.

#### Subchannel A. A Prepared Dwelling Is Cleared for Posture
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A dwelling is assigned, purified, and occupied by bodies circling, standing, bowing, and prostrating.
- Active motifs: prepared dwelling `quranic:root_000161:B001/m01`; house `quranic:root_000166:B001/m01`; purification `quranic:root_000953:B001/m01`; ritual circuit `quranic:root_000957:B001/m01`; standing `quranic:root_001273:B002/m01`; bowing `quranic:root_000594:B001/m01`; prostration `quranic:root_000675:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:26 `ب و ء`, `ب ي ت`, `ط ه ر`, `ط و ف`, `ق و م`, `ر ك ع`, `س ج د`
- Synthesis: Purification is spatial preparation for coordinated movement. The cleared House receives four distinct bodily operations, making sanctity an ordered use of place.

#### Subchannel B. Proclamation Draws Bodies Through Depth
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A public call mobilizes walkers and lean mounts through remote, deep mountain passes toward the center.
- Active motifs: public proclamation `quranic:root_000022:B003/m01`; pilgrimage to a revered center `quranic:root_000295:B001/m01`; walking on foot `quranic:root_000546:B003/m01`; lean trained mount `quranic:root_000914:B001/m01`; wide mountain pass `quranic:root_001131:B001/m01`; depth and distance `quranic:root_001045:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:27 `ء ذ ن`, `ح ج ج`, `ر ج ل`, `ض م ر`, `ف ج ج`, `ع م ق`
- Synthesis: The call is answered as a geography of effort. Human feet, conditioned animals, and deep passes form one convergence scene in which remoteness is actively crossed.

#### Subchannel C. Attendance Becomes Witnessing and Provision
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Arriving participants witness benefit, name God over provision, and convert animal sustenance into food for self and distressed poor.
- Active motifs: witnessed presence `quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`; benefit `quranic:root_001536:B001/m01`; naming aloud `quranic:root_000516:B004/m01`; allotted provision `quranic:root_000560:B001/m01`; eating `quranic:root_000043:B001/m01`; feeding `quranic:root_000934:B002/m01`; straitened livelihood `quranic:root_000079:B002/m01`; material need `quranic:root_001169:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:28 `ش ه د`, `ن ف ع`, `ذ ك ر`, `ر ز ق`, `ء ك ل`, `ط ع م`, `ب ء س`, `ف ق ر`
- Synthesis: Presence at the sanctuary becomes socially productive. Witnessing benefit and naming the source of provision culminate in a meal whose recipient structure includes the afflicted poor.

#### Subchannel D. Completion Is Marked on Body and Route
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Pilgrims complete bodily grooming, discharge binding vows, and close the movement with a circuit around the ancient House.
- Active motifs: finishing and completion `quranic:root_001237:B004/m01`; removal of grooming grime `quranic:root_000183:B001/m01`; full discharge of an obligation `quranic:root_001669:B001/m01`; vow `quranic:root_001488:B002/m01`; ritual circuit `quranic:root_000957:B001/m01`; ancient standing `quranic:root_000979:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:29 `ق ض ي`, `ت ف ث`, `و ف ي`, `ن ذ ر`, `ط و ف`, `ع ت ق`
- Synthesis: Completion is registered twice: the body sheds its temporary condition, and movement closes in a circuit. Vows are not abstract intentions but obligations discharged through this terminal sequence.

### 7. P2 (22:19-37) - Marked Animal Bodies Become Shared Provision
- Semantic invariant: Consecrated bodies pass through naming, alignment, collapse, distribution, and a final separation of material from moral reach.

- Active motifs: enacted parable `quranic:root_000906:B003/m01`; attentive hearing `quranic:root_000741:B003/m01`; creating `quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`; fly `quranic:root_000507:B001/m01`; collective assembly `quranic:root_000259:B001/m01`; stripping or seizure `quranic:root_000727:B001/m01`; recovery and rescue `quranic:root_001540:B001/m01`; weakness `quranic:root_000909:B001/m01`; seeker or quest `quranic:root_000943:B001/m01`; true measure `quranic:root_001205:B001/m01`; strength `quranic:root_001274:B001/m01`; might `quranic:root_001008:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:73 `ض ر ب`, `م ث ل`, `س م ع`, `خ ل ق`, `ذ ب ب`, `ج م ع`, `س ل ب`, `ن ق ذ`, `ض ع ف`, `ط ل ب`; 22:74 `ق د ر`, `ق و ي`, `ع ز ز`
- Synthesis: The parable tests power through custody at the smallest scale. Failure occurs twice, first in production and then in retrieval, so inability to master one weak creature exposes the false measure behind the cult.

### 16. P4 (22:58-78) - A Selected Community Becomes an Embodied Witness
- Semantic invariant: Selection forms a relay whose members receive, bow, cultivate, strive, testify, and hold fast under one patron.
- Surface relation: direct; 22:75-78 anchors selection of messengers, knowledge before and behind, return of affairs, bowing, prostration, worship, good work, striving, lack of constriction, communal naming, testimony, prayer, alms, and protective attachment.
- Surprising reach: Witnesshood is not merely verbal. It is assembled from bodily postures, agricultural success, unobstructed exertion, inherited naming, and a graspable tether to a patron.

#### Subchannel A. Selection Establishes a Message Relay
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Selected messengers carry communication under comprehensive hearing and sight, while what lies before and behind them returns to one authority.
- Active motifs: selection `quranic:root_000873:B002/m01`; messenger and message `quranic:root_000563:B002/m01`; hearing `quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`; sight `quranic:root_000121:B001/m01`; what lies ahead `quranic:root_001693:B008/m01`; what lies behind `quranic:root_000433:B002/m01`; return `quranic:root_000544:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:75 `ص ف و`, `ر س ل`, `س م ع`, `ب ص ر`; 22:76 `ي د ي`, `خ ل ف`, `ر ج ع`
- Synthesis: Selection places messengers within a supervised chain rather than granting autonomous possession of the message. Their temporal horizon and the affairs they carry remain enclosed by knowledge and return.

#### Subchannel B. Worship Cultivates a Field of Success
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Bowing, prostration, service, and beneficial action work the ground like cultivation whose yield is survival and success.
- Active motifs: bowing `quranic:root_000594:B001/m01`; prostration `quranic:root_000675:B001/m01`; worship and service `quranic:root_000973:B003/m01`; smoothed and tamed path `quranic:root_000973:B005/m01`; beneficial action `quranic:root_000452:B001/m01`; splitting soil `quranic:root_001175:B001/m01`; farmer or plougher `quranic:root_001175:B003/m01`; success and survival `quranic:root_001175:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:77 `ر ك ع`, `س ج د`, `ع ب د`, `ف ع ل`, `خ ي ر`, `ف ل ح`
- Synthesis: The cluster gives worship an agricultural operation. Repeated lowering works and opens the self as soil is worked, while good action is the cultivation whose harvest is flourishing.

#### Subchannel C. Striving Crosses Hard Ground Without Constriction
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Exertion reaches its limit across exposed hard terrain but is not trapped in thicket-like congestion because the community has been gathered and chosen.
- Active motifs: exertion to the limit `quranic:root_000268:B001/m01`; exposed hard ground `quranic:root_000268:B004/m01`; selection and drawing near `quranic:root_000220:B004/m01`; thicket or congestion `quranic:root_000304:B001/m01`; constriction `quranic:root_000304:B002/m01`; obedient religious order `quranic:root_000504:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:78 `ج ه د`, `ج ب ي`, `ح ر ج`, `د ي ن`
- Synthesis: Striving is strenuous without being maze-like. Selection draws the community near, while the lexical terrain distinguishes exposed difficulty, which can be crossed, from dense obstruction, which has been removed from the religious path.

#### Subchannel D. The Named Witness Body Holds a Patronal Strap
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An inherited creed names a whole community, positions messenger and people as reciprocal witnesses, and secures prayer and alms through attachment to a patron-helper.
- Active motifs: creed `quranic:root_001445:B003/m01`; father and nurturer `quranic:root_000007:B001/m01`; naming `quranic:root_000745:B005/m01`; wholeness and safety `quranic:root_000737:B001/m01`; witnessed presence `quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`; testimony `quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`; prayer `quranic:root_000879:B003/m01`; growth-giving alms `quranic:root_000637:B001/m01`; holding fast for protection `quranic:root_001021:B001/m01`; graspable rope or strap `quranic:root_001021:B002/m01`; patronage and support `quranic:root_001684:B004/m01`; aid and victory `quranic:root_001510:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:78 `م ل ل`, `ء ب و`, `س م و`, `س ل م`, `ش ه د`, `ق و م`, `ص ل و`, `ز ك و`, `ع ص م`, `و ل ي`, `ن ص ر`
- Synthesis: Communal identity is made durable through naming, ancestry, reciprocal testimony, and maintained practice. Holding fast then turns patronage into a physical relation: the witness body remains whole by gripping the support that also protects it.

## Standalone Subchannels

### S1. P1 (22:12-13) - Near Harm Masquerades as Patronage
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A claimant calls on a supposedly close patron whose harm is nearer than benefit and whose intimate or clan relation fails.
- Active motifs: calling `quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`; claim and attribution `quranic:root_000478:B002/m01`; harm `quranic:root_000907:B001/m01`; benefit `quranic:root_001536:B001/m01`; nearness `quranic:root_001212:B001/m01`; patronage and support `quranic:root_001684:B004/m01`; intimate association `quranic:root_001016:B012/m01`; clan relation `quranic:root_001016:B013/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:12-13 `د ع و`, `ض ر ر`, `ن ف ع`, `ق ر ب`, `و ل ي`, `ع ش ر`
- Synthesis: Invocation constructs a false social frame of proximity and aid. The surprising pressure is that closeness itself is inverted: harm is what arrives, while patron and clan prove bad precisely where protection was expected.

### S2. P1 (22:14) - Entry Opens Into a Flowing Garden
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Faithful action is answered by admission into concealed growth through which watercourses run beneath.
- Active motifs: entry `quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`; hidden garden `quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`; flowing movement `quranic:root_000240:B001/m01`; river or channel `quranic:root_001559:B001/m01`; intended action `quranic:root_001167:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:14 `د خ ل`, `ج ن ن`, `ج ر ي`, `ن ه ر`, `ف ع ل`
- Synthesis: Reward is a spatial transition from action into a living enclosure. Concealment by growth and visible flow make the garden both shelter and continuously supplied habitat.

### S3. P2 (22:25) - Equal Sanctuary Access Is Guarded Against Lateral Deviation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A bounded sanctuary equalizes resident and outsider while blocking anyone who tries to turn access sideways through wrongdoing.
- Active motifs: blocking and turning away `quranic:root_000848:B001/m01`; road `quranic:root_000672:B001/m01`; mosque `quranic:root_000675:B002/m01`; sanctuary boundary `quranic:root_000313:B003/m01`; equality `quranic:root_000766:B001/m01`; settled residence `quranic:root_001038:B001/m01`; outsider or desert visitor `quranic:root_000097:B002/m01`; lateral deviation `quranic:root_001345:B001/m01`; wrongful misplacement `quranic:root_000967:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:25 `ص د د`, `س ب ل`, `س ج د`, `ح ر م`, `س و ي`, `ع ك ف`, `ب د و`, `ل ح د`, `ظ ل م`
- Synthesis: The sanctuary combines boundedness with equal standing. Its boundary does not authorize local possession; instead, it protects a common route against obstruction and crooked appropriation.

### S4. P2 (22:31) - Polytheistic Fall Becomes Prey and Windblown Debris
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Loss of exclusive orientation becomes a fall from the sky, followed by either a bird's snatch or a wind-driven plunge into remoteness.
- Active motifs: directional inclination `quranic:root_000362:B002/m01`; hunter's snare `quranic:root_000791:B006/m01`; falling from height `quranic:root_000402:B001/m01`; swift snatching `quranic:root_000423:B001/m01`; bird in flight `quranic:root_000962:B001/m01`; plunging into an abyss `quranic:root_001609:B002/m01`; wind `quranic:root_000609:B003/m01`; remoteness `quranic:root_000683:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:31 `ح ن ف`, `ش ر ك`, `خ ر ر`, `س م و`, `خ ط ف`, `ط ي ر`, `ه و ي`, `ر و ح`, `س ح ق`
- Synthesis: The verse offers two terminal mechanics for an unanchored body: predation or dispersal. In both, the fallen person loses agency immediately and becomes material handled by stronger motion.

### S5. P3 (22:55-57) - A Sterile Deadline Closes Doubt
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Persistent uncertainty is terminated by a sudden, barren day, after which adjudication separates gardened flourishing from humiliation.
- Active motifs: doubt `quranic:root_001416:B004/m01`; sudden arrival `quranic:root_000135:B001/m01`; barren womb `quranic:root_001037:B001/m01`; sterile wind `quranic:root_001037:B002/m01`; lethal barren conflict `quranic:root_001037:B005/m01`; kingdom `quranic:root_001444:B003/m01`; adjudication `quranic:root_000348:B002/m01`; hidden garden `quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`; flourishing condition `quranic:root_001525:B001/m01`; humiliation `quranic:root_001608:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:55 `م ر ي`, `ب غ ت`, `ع ق م`; 22:56 `م ل ك`, `ح ك م`, `ج ن ن`, `ن ع م`; 22:57 `ه و ن`
- Synthesis: Barrenness describes a deadline that produces no further opportunity. Its sudden arrival sterilizes ongoing doubt, and judgment then restores fertility only on the garden side of the separation.

### S6. P4 (22:60) - Measured Retaliation Is Surpassed by Erasure
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Injury is answered in equivalent measure; renewed aggression triggers redress, while pardon and covering remove the remaining trace.
- Active motifs: retaliation `quranic:root_001033:B007/m01`; equivalence `quranic:root_001397:B001/m01`; transgressive overreach `quranic:root_000138:B003/m01`; redress and vindication `quranic:root_001510:B002/m01`; erasing pardon `quranic:root_001032:B001/m01`; erasure of a trace `quranic:root_001032:B006/m01`; protective covering `quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`; covering a wrong `quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:60 `ع ق ب`, `م ث ل`, `ب غ ي`, `ن ص ر`, `ع ف و`, `غ ف ر`
- Synthesis: Equivalence limits the first response, but the scene does not end with balanced force. Redress is enclosed by two operations that go further than repayment: erasing the offense's trace and covering what would otherwise remain exposed.

### S7. Whole-Surah - Arrow Lots Partition a Camel by Chance
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A receptacle holds gaming arrows; players wager for dominance and reputation, then use the lots to divide a slaughtered camel.
- Active motifs: receptacle holding gaming arrows `quranic:root_000532:B010/m01`; wagering and victory by deception `quranic:root_001255:B007/m01`; prestige contest in generosity `quranic:root_001294:B006/m01`; players, arrow lots, and partition of a camel `quranic:root_001694:B007/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:1 `ر ب ب`; 22:18 `ق م ر`, `ك ر م`; 22:70 `ي س ر`
- Synthesis: The cluster forms a complete rival allocation rite: equipment, players, competitive motive, animal stake, and distribution rule. It usefully pressures the primary sacrificial reading in 22:34-37, where animal flesh is assigned through divine naming, piety, and feeding rather than chance, deception, and status competition.

### S8. Whole-Surah - Milking Depends on Remnant, Interval, and Let-Down
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A full udder retains a small remnant, refills between milkings, releases milk under massage, and can finally fail or dry up.
- Active motifs: full udder and abundant yield `quranic:root_000810:B003/m01`; remnant milk left to summon the next flow `quranic:root_000478:B003/m01`; milk returning between sessions `quranic:root_001188:B006/m01`; massage that induces let-down `quranic:root_001416:B001/m01`; successive flowing milk `quranic:root_000563:B006/m01`; depleted udder `quranic:root_000683:B005/m01`; milk that fails to persist `quranic:root_001290:B006/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:36 `ش ك ر`; 22:12 `د ع و`; 22:19 `ف و ق`; 22:55 `م ر ي`; 22:52 `ر س ل`; 22:31 `س ح ق`; 22:42 `ك ذ ب`
- Synthesis: The motifs form one husbandry cycle of reserve, waiting, stimulation, yield, and depletion. This materializes the surah's primary language of nursing, provision, and gratitude: sustenance renews through a timed relation that must be tended and can cease, rather than through autonomous possession.

### S9. Whole-Surah - A Working Well Is a Coordinated Machine

### S10. Whole-Surah - A Camel Saddle Distributes Load Through Layers

### S11. Whole-Surah - A Garment Is Woven, Fulled, Stitched, and Lined

### S13. Whole-Surah P1-P4 Bridge - Descent Exposes the Receiving Medium
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Repeated scene signature with contrast across P1, P2, P3, and P4: something passes from above or outside into a receiving body, ground, or heart, and the receiver converts the arrival into growth, guidance, or dissolution.
- Active motifs: descending rain `quranic:root_001492:B001/m01`; descending revelation `quranic:root_001492:B002/m01`; pouring from above `quranic:root_000838:B001/m01`; smelting by heat `quranic:root_000888:B002/m01`; receiving recitation `quranic:root_001372:B011/m01`; low receptive ground `quranic:root_000385:B001/m01`; fertile green earth `quranic:root_000025:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:5 `ن ز ل`; 22:16 `ن ز ل`; 22:19 `ص ب ب`; 22:20 `ص ه ر`; 22:52 `ل ق ي`; 22:54 `خ ب ت`; 22:63 `ن ز ل`, `ء ر ض`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P1 "Dormant Earth Swells Into Display" and "Descending Signs Open a Path," P2 "The Body Becomes a Smelting Vessel," P3 "The Message Is Released Into Recitation" and "Knowledge Settles the Heart Like Receptive Ground," and P4 "Water Converts Earth Into Green Surface." The bridge is the repeated transfer into a medium, sharpened by contrast: rain and revelation materialize latent life or guidance in receptive ground, while poured heat liquefies the exposed body. This reframes reception as an active conversion whose outcome discloses the condition of what receives.

### S14. P1 and P4 Bridge - Attachment Reverses From Snare to Support
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Reversal between P1 and P4: an attachment chosen under false patronage constricts and misdirects, while attachment to the rightful patron prevents separation and bears the witness body.
- Active motifs: patronage and support `quranic:root_001684:B004/m01`; rope, means, or connection `quranic:root_000664:B003/m01`; choking by a cut cord `quranic:root_001240:B009/m01`; holding fast for protection `quranic:root_001021:B001/m01`; graspable rope or strap `quranic:root_001021:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:4 `و ل ي`; 22:15 `س ب ب`, `ق ط ع`; 22:78 `ع ص م`, `و ل ي`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P1 "Patronage Scripts a Route Toward Fire" and "The Escape Device Tightens on Its Maker," and P4 "The Named Witness Body Holds a Patronal Strap." The bridge is a mechanical reversal in the function of attachment: the false bond conducts and chokes, whereas the protected bond supplies a grip and keeps the communal body whole. This materializes patronage as a load-bearing relation whose truth is tested by what its tether does to the attached body.

### S15. P2 and P3 Bridge - Built Places Pass Through a Functional Lifecycle
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Causal sequence and contrast across P2 and P3: a dwelling is prepared and cleared for coordinated use, defended from demolition, maintained through practice, or left as a collapsed shell when use and care cease.
- Active motifs: prepared dwelling `quranic:root_000161:B001/m01`; purification `quranic:root_000953:B001/m01`; demolition of a building `quranic:root_001581:B001/m01`; establishing and maintaining `quranic:root_001273:B004/m01`; abandoned nonfunction `quranic:root_001027:B001/m01`; structural collapse `quranic:root_000450:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:26 `ب و ء`, `ط ه ر`; 22:40 `ه د م`; 22:41 `ق و م`; 22:45 `ع ط ل`, `خ و ي`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P2 "A Prepared Dwelling Is Cleared for Posture," P3 "Expulsion Exposes a Network of Sacred Buildings" and "Survival Becomes Institutional Cultivation," and P3 "Infrastructure Remains After Its Community Fails." The bridge is a functional lifecycle: preparation enables ordered use, counterforce preserves that use, maintenance renews it, and abandonment separates structure from function. This supports the sacred-place reading by locating sanctity in sustained communal operation rather than inert possession.

### S16. P1, P2, and P4 Bridge - Witnessed Presence Becomes Assigned Testimony
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Role progression across P1, P2, and P4: communities first stand under a witnessing judgment, participants then witness benefit through attendance, and the selected community finally receives an enduring testimony-bearing role.
- Active motifs: witnessed presence `quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`; testimony and declaration `quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`; realized benefit `quranic:root_001536:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:17 `ش ه د`; 22:28 `ش ه د`, `ن ف ع`; 22:78 `ش ه د`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P1 "Witnessed Judgment Separates Communities," P2 "Attendance Becomes Witnessing and Provision," and P4 "The Named Witness Body Holds a Patronal Strap." The bridge is a role progression from being present before judgment, through present participation in benefit, to bearing testimony before others. This supports the surah's witness reading by making testimony the mature obligation of accountable and socially productive presence.

### S17. P1 and P3 Bridge - Trial Assays Concealed Composition
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Repeated scene signature across P1 and P3: an incoming disturbance acts as an assay, and the response reveals an inward condition that ordinary stability had concealed.
- Active motifs: assay of a person or metal `quranic:root_001128:B001/m01`; calamity striking `quranic:root_000889:B004/m01`; flipping the face `quranic:root_001248:B004/m01`; disease or deviation from health `quranic:root_001415:B001/m01`; hardened heart `quranic:root_001227:B002/m01`; low receptive ground `quranic:root_000385:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:11 `ف ت ن`, `ص و ب`, `ق ل ب`; 22:53 `ف ت ن`, `م ر ض`, `ق س و`; 22:54 `خ ب ت`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P1 "Edge Worship Flips Like a Failed Trade," and P3 "The Insertion Assays Diseased and Stone-Hard Hearts" and "Knowledge Settles the Heart Like Receptive Ground." The bridge is the assay function shared by calamity and hostile insertion: neither disturbance is merely an external injury, because each separates conditional instability or hardness from receptive humility. This usefully reframes trial as disclosure of material already present in the worshipper or heart.

### S18. P3 and P4 Bridge - Counterforce Tightens From Permission to Measure and Pardon
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Shared invariant and causal progression across P3 and P4: force enters only after aggression, remains bounded by its protective or equivalent function, and opens beyond redress into pardon.
- Active motifs: repelling and protecting `quranic:root_000480:B001/m01`; permission `quranic:root_000022:B004/m01`; grievance requiring redress `quranic:root_000967:B003/m01`; retaliation `quranic:root_001033:B007/m01`; equivalence `quranic:root_001397:B001/m01`; transgressive overreach `quranic:root_000138:B003/m01`; redress and vindication `quranic:root_001510:B002/m01`; erasing pardon `quranic:root_001032:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:38 `د ف ع`; 22:39 `ء ذ ن`, `ظ ل م`; 22:60 `ع ق ب`, `م ث ل`, `ب غ ي`, `ن ص ر`, `ع ف و`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P3 "Permission Activates Protective Counterforce" and P4 "Measured Retaliation Is Surpassed by Erasure." The bridge is one legal grammar at two scales: communal defense repels prior expulsion, while individual redress answers injury only in equivalent measure before pardon removes its trace. This supports the primary reading by defining legitimate force through prior wrong, proportional response, and a restorative horizon.

### S19. P1, P2, and P4 Bridge - Directed Passage Culminates in Provisioned Entry
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Repeated scene signature with role progression across P1, P2, and P4: faithful action or difficult travel crosses a boundary into a supplied interior, and the entrance converts promise into inhabited satisfaction.
- Active motifs: intended action `quranic:root_001167:B001/m01`; entry `quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`; hidden garden `quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`; flowing movement `quranic:root_000240:B001/m01`; migration `quranic:root_001578:B002/m01`; allotted provision `quranic:root_000560:B001/m01`; satisfaction `quranic:root_000569:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:14 `ف ع ل`, `د خ ل`, `ج ن ن`, `ج ر ي`; 22:23 `د خ ل`, `ج ن ن`, `ج ر ي`; 22:58 `ه ج ر`, `ر ز ق`; 22:59 `د خ ل`, `ر ض و`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P1 "Entry Opens Into a Flowing Garden," P2 "The Garden Fits an Honored Appearance," and P4 "Exile and Death Remain a Directed Journey" and "Provision Culminates in a Satisfying Entrance." The bridge is the repeated terminal operation of entry: action first receives a destination, the destination becomes a fitted habitation, and even migration interrupted by death still reaches reception. This supports the surah's journey reading by making provisioned arrival, not uninterrupted travel, the measure of completion.

### S20. P1 and P4 Bridge - Plural Practice Persists Until Common Adjudication
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Shared invariant and causal sequence between P1 and P4: communities remain distinct in affiliation and embodied rite, while their difference is carried intact into separation by a common judgment.
- Active motifs: communal people `quranic:root_001273:B001/m01`; judicial separation `quranic:root_001159:B002/m01`; community joined by a common matter `quranic:root_000053:B004/m01`; assigned worship form `quranic:root_001498:B001/m01`; concrete ritual work `quranic:root_001498:B003/m01`; adjudication `quranic:root_000348:B002/m01`; separation between parties `quranic:root_000170:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:17 `ق و م`, `ف ص ل`; 22:67 `ء م م`, `ن س ك`; 22:69 `ح ك م`, `ب ي ن`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P1 "Witnessed Judgment Separates Communities" and P4 "Each Community Receives an Assigned Rite" and "Argument Is Transferred to Judgment." The bridge is not plurality alone but its judicial sequence: communal distinction persists as practiced form, contention does not erase it, and one authority finally separates the disputed claims. This supports the surah's treatment of ritual difference as embodied and accountable rather than either flattened or autonomous.

### S21. P3 and P4 Bridge - Hostility Moves From Interpolation to Bodily Assault
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Repeated scene signature with role progression across P3 and P4: recited signs provoke an attempt to control transmission, first by casting foreign material into the recitation and then by nearly seizing the reciter.
- Active motifs: messenger and message `quranic:root_000563:B002/m01`; voiced recitation `quranic:root_001450:B007/m01`; hostile casting `quranic:root_001372:B005/m01`; erasing and replacing `quranic:root_001495:B001/m01`; securing and establishing `quranic:root_000348:B004/m01`; following and recitation `quranic:root_000186:B001/m01`; manifest signs `quranic:root_000074:B003/m01`; violent assault `quranic:root_005351:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:52 `ر س ل`, `م ن ي`, `ل ق ي`, `ن س خ`, `ح ك م`; 22:72 `ت ل و`, `ء ي ي`, `س ط و`
- Synthesis: Canonical placements are P3 "The Message Is Released Into Recitation" and "Hostile Insertion Is Erased While the Text Is Secured," and P4 "Recitation Provokes an Assaulting Face." The bridge is a progression in the attack surface: interference first enters the voiced text, then shifts toward the body voicing it, while neither operation gains custody of the signs. This usefully pressures the revelation reading by distinguishing vulnerable transmitters and hostile channels from the secured message they fail to master.

### S22. Whole-Surah - A Difficult Birth Recruits Receiving and Extracting Hands
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Labor approaches, a child presents hands first, a birth attendant receives the emerging body, and dangerous obstruction calls for manual extraction before afterbirth signs and uterine pain mark the postpartum condition.
- Active motifs: approaching labor `quranic:root_001212:B012/m01`; hands-first presentation `quranic:root_001630:B010/m01`; birth attendant receiving the child `quranic:root_001198:B007/m01`; emergency extraction from the womb `quranic:root_005351:B004/m01`; afterbirth signs `quranic:root_000822:B006/m01`; uterine pain after delivery `quranic:root_000552:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:13 `ق ر ب`; 22:72 `و ج ه`, `س ط و`; 22:42 `ق ب ل`; 22:17 `ش ه د`; 22:5 `ر ح م`
- Synthesis: The motifs form one difficult-delivery sequence from onset through malpresentation, assistance, extraction, and postpartum complication. This materializes the pregnancies released in 22:2 and the gestational stages of 22:5 as a hazardous relational passage: laying down a burden may require skilled hands, and emergence does not end bodily vulnerability.

### S23. Whole-Surah - A Sluice Network Converts Stored Water Into Crop Flow
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Rain or well water gathers in a reservoir, enters a directed watercourse, is rationed through a dam or sluice, and disperses through outlets toward cultivated ground.
- Active motifs: reservoir collecting and releasing water `quranic:root_000016:B007/m01`; directed watercourse into a basin `quranic:root_000009:B004/m01`; runoff channels and outlets `quranic:root_000480:B006/m01`; dam opened to the needed measure `quranic:root_000751:B007/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:5 `ء ج ل`; 22:7 `ء ت ي`; 22:38 `د ف ع`; 22:47 `س ن و`
- Synthesis: Storage, direction, measured release, and dispersal make one irrigation mechanism rather than a general water cluster. It materializes the rain-to-green-earth readings of 22:5 and 22:63 and usefully reframes the abandoned well of 22:45: provision persists when water is gathered and circulated through an operative system.

### S24. Whole-Surah - A Sacrificial Hide Becomes Hair-On Leather and Straps
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: An animal is skinned, tree bark supplies tanning material, the hide dries with its hair retained, and the finished leather is cut into straps.
- Active motifs: skinning a camel and taking its hide `quranic:root_000253:B005/m01`; tanning bark `quranic:root_000737:B008/m01`; dried hair-on hide `quranic:root_001021:B006/m01`; cut leather straps `quranic:root_000769:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:20 `ج ل د`; 22:34 `س ل م`; 22:78 `ع ص م`; 22:46 `س ي ر`
- Synthesis: The sequence carries an animal covering through removal, chemical treatment, drying, and fabrication. This materializes the witnessed benefits and bodily provision of 22:28 and 22:36-37 beyond meat: the consecrated animal can enter durable human use without collapsing the rite into consumption alone.

### S25. Whole-Surah - Contracted Labor Moves From Bondage Into Legal Solidarity
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: An enslaved worker under uncompensated labor enters a written installment contract, earns the price of release, becomes free, and retains a defined patronal bond after emancipation.
- Active motifs: enslaved status `quranic:root_000973:B001/m01`; compelled labor without wages `quranic:root_000685:B002/m01`; written manumission contract `quranic:root_001283:B005/m01`; labor earning the price of freedom `quranic:root_000709:B005/m01`; emancipation from bondage `quranic:root_000979:B001/m01`; legal patronage after manumission `quranic:root_001684:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:77 `ع ب د`; 22:36 `س خ ر`; 22:70 `ك ت ب`; 22:51 `س ع ي`; 22:29 `ع ت ق`; 22:78 `و ل ي`
- Synthesis: Status, coercion, contract, earned installments, release, and continuing legal relation form one social progression. It reframes the opposed forms of striving and patronage in 22:51 and 22:78: effort can serve domination or become a measured route out of it, while rightful patronage persists as a recognized legal bond rather than ownership.

### S26. Whole-Surah - An Earth Oven Makes Fire Hold Still Long Enough to Feed
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A baker digs an earthen oven, closes it with a fitted cover, banks fuel in the soil to retain heat, and turns bread in hot ash.
- Active motifs: dug earth oven `quranic:root_000708:B009/m01`; fitted oven cover `quranic:root_001669:B005/m01`; fire banked in earth `quranic:root_001424:B008/m01`; bread cooked in hot ash `quranic:root_001445:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:4 `س ع ر`; 22:29 `و ف ي`; 22:65 `م س ك`; 22:78 `م ل ل`
- Synthesis: Excavation, closure, heat retention, and cooking form a bounded transformation of fire into food. This usefully pressures the consuming and smelting fire of 22:19-22: controlled heat preserves its container and nourishes, whereas punitive heat crosses the body's boundary and destroys container and contents together.

### S27. Whole-Surah - A Spear Is Fitted, Aimed, Thrust, and Made to Penetrate
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A point is fixed to a shaft, the weapon is directed and moved into readiness, opposing spears interlock, and a straight thrust reaches the interior.
- Active motifs: fitting a spearhead to its shaft `quranic:root_000051:B011/m01`; aiming a spear at its target `quranic:root_000161:B007/m01`; moving or shaking the spear `quranic:root_001588:B001/m01`; interlocked spears and thrusting `quranic:root_000777:B003/m01`; straight penetrating wound `quranic:root_000347:B009/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:41 `ء م ر`; 22:26 `ب و ء`; 22:5 `ه ز ز`; 22:18 `ش ج ر`; 22:40 `ح ق ق`
- Synthesis: Assembly, aim, mobilization, contact, and penetration make force a deliberate apparatus with an ordered endpoint. This materializes the defensive counterforce of 22:38-40 and sharpens its need for permission and proportion: violence is prepared and directed through discrete human operations, not an unbounded impulse.

### S28. Whole-Surah - A Horse Race Can Be Won by Pace or Corrupted by a Spare Horse
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A rider extends the rein to accelerate through a known gait, competitors strive for precedence, the runner-up follows the winner, a prize awaits, and an additional horse led alongside creates a prohibited advantage.
- Active motifs: rider extending the rein for speed `quranic:root_000151:B007/m01`; controlled racing gait `quranic:root_001212:B014/m01`; competitive striving `quranic:root_000709:B008/m01`; second horse behind the winner `quranic:root_000879:B006/m01`; race prize `quranic:root_001625:B007/m01`; prohibited spare-horse tactic `quranic:root_000262:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:5 `ب ل غ`; 22:13 `ق ر ب`; 22:51 `س ع ي`; 22:35 `ص ل و`; 22:36 `و ج ب`, `ج ن ب`
- Synthesis: Rider, gait, competition, finish order, stake, and cheating device form a regulated contest rather than a generic game. It usefully pressures the surah's opposed strivings: speed toward a goal can remain legible and rule-bound, or an extraneous advantage can turn striving into the frustrated contest against the signs in 22:51.

### S29. Whole-Surah - A Blood Claim Is Bounded by Retaliation, Payment, or Waiver
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A killing or wound generates a claim that may be answered blood for blood, converted into compensatory payment, assessed as wound damages, or relinquished without further pursuit.
- Active motifs: blood-for-blood retaliation `quranic:root_000161:B004/m01`; blood money replacing retaliation `quranic:root_001036:B004/m01`; assessed compensation for a wound `quranic:root_001488:B003/m01`; waived or unpursued blood claim `quranic:root_001581:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:26 `ب و ء`; 22:46 `ع ق ل`; 22:29 `ن ذ ر`; 22:40 `ه د م`
- Synthesis: Injury, claim, equivalent response, substitute payment, and waiver form a finite social process rather than an open-ended feud. This materializes the grammar of 22:60: redress acknowledges harm, equivalence limits response, and relinquishment makes pardon a concrete alternative to continued retaliation.

### S30. Whole-Surah - Stored Oil Becomes a Lamp's Usable Light
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Illuminating oil is held in a dedicated vessel, fed into a lamp, and converted into visible light.
- Active motifs: oil vessel `quranic:root_000457:B010/m01`; oil used for illumination `quranic:root_000732:B005/m01`; lamp and lamp-holder `quranic:root_000839:B005/m01`; produced light `quranic:root_001564:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:18 `د ب ب`; 22:71 `س ل ط`; 22:63 `ص ب ح`; 22:72 `ن و ر`
- Synthesis: Vessel, fuel, instrument, and luminous outcome form one compact conversion mechanism. It reframes the surah's fire and manifest-sign readings: combustion can be contained and made perceptible as guidance, in contrast to the fitted fire of 22:19-22 that consumes the body it surrounds.

### S31. Whole-Surah - Burial Builds a Side Chamber for the Concealed Body
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: The dead body is concealed in a grave understood as a house and placed within a niche cut into the grave's side.
- Active motifs: grave as the dead person's house `quranic:root_000166:B007/m01`; burial and concealment of the dead `quranic:root_000266:B009/m01`; side niche cut for the body `quranic:root_001345:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:26 `ب ي ت`; 22:14 `ج ن ن`; 22:25 `ل ح د`
- Synthesis: Body, enclosure, and fitted side chamber form a deliberate housing operation. This materializes resurrection in 22:7 and the death-journey of 22:58-59 as reversals of constructed concealment: raising and received entry overcome a dwelling made to keep the dead body out of sight.

### S32. Whole-Surah - A Probed Wound Can Suppurate, Close, and Relapse
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A practitioner probes a deep wound, tracks swelling and pus as corruption spreads, observes flesh close over it, and confronts renewed disease after apparent improvement.
- Active motifs: probing and treating a head wound `quranic:root_000295:B004/m01`; wound swelling into corruption `quranic:root_000138:B004/m01`; extending suppuration `quranic:root_001407:B007/m01`; flesh closing over the wound `quranic:root_001348:B008/m01`; relapse after improvement `quranic:root_001096:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:27 `ح ج ج`; 22:60 `ب غ ي`; 22:15 `م د د`; 22:37 `ل ح م`; 22:50 `غ ف ر`
- Synthesis: Diagnosis, spreading corruption, suppuration, closure, and relapse form one clinical course in which surface repair may not equal cure. This usefully pressures the diseased-heart assay of 22:53-54: disturbance can expose a pathology whose depth must be tested, and apparent closure does not prove that the inward condition has healed.

### S33. Whole-Surah - Mourning Removes Ornament and Replaces It With Recurring Attendance
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A bereaved woman suspends adornment, bares the places normally carrying jewelry, wears black mourning clothes, and receives repeated condolence visits.
- Active motifs: mourning abstention from adornment `quranic:root_000002:B007/m01`; black mourning garments `quranic:root_000727:B003/m01`; neck and jewelry places left bare `quranic:root_001027:B002/m01`; recurring condolence attendance `quranic:root_001058:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:21 `ح د د`; 22:73 `س ل ب`; 22:45 `ع ط ل`; 22:22 `ع و د`
- Synthesis: Bereaved role, removed ornament, substitute dress, and returning visitors form one public rite of loss. It reframes the surah's clothing contrast and death journey: garden adornment makes honored arrival visible, while mourning marks departure through subtraction and turns an individual death into a repeated communal attendance.

### S34. Whole-Surah - Hospitality Turns Prepared Provision Into a Shared Meal
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A host prepares food for an arriving guest, gathers it in a serving vessel, sets it on a cloth or in a heap, and assigns an edible portion.
- Active motifs: feeding and honoring a guest `quranic:root_001222:B003/m01`; food-gathering serving vessel `quranic:root_001222:B004/m01`; table cloth and heaped food `quranic:root_000840:B011/m01`; provision prepared for an arrival `quranic:root_001492:B005/m01`; allotted edible portion `quranic:root_000043:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:45 `ق ر ي`; 22:35 `ص ب ر`; 22:63 `ن ز ل`; 22:28 `ء ك ل`
- Synthesis: Host, guest, prepared food, vessel, serving surface, and portion form one reception scene. This materializes the commands to feed in 22:28 and 22:36 and the provisioned entrance of 22:58-59: sustenance becomes welcome only when it is prepared, set before another, and apportioned for use.

### S35. Whole-Surah - Honey Moves From Hive and Comb Through Tool Into Storage
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A beekeeper works at the hive entrance, takes honey still held in comb, uses an extraction tool, and stores the yield in large skins.
- Active motifs: hive entrance `quranic:root_001682:B003/m01`; honey held in comb before pressing `quranic:root_000822:B007/m01`; honey-extraction tool `quranic:root_001489:B010/m01`; large skins for stored honey `quranic:root_001625:B009/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 22:61 `و ل ج`; 22:28 `ش ه د`; 22:67 `ن ز ع`; 22:36 `و ج ب`
- Synthesis: Hive, comb, extractor, operator, and storage vessel form a complete harvest chain. It supports the sacrificial provision reading and usefully pressures the fly parable of 22:73: a tiny creature participates in an ordered production that humans can harvest and preserve, while the invoked powers cannot create even a fly or recover what it takes.
